title: Hemoglobin–RDW coupling provides no clear cross-cycle improvement in resting pulse prediction beyond flexible routine measures
abstract: We tested whether a source-standardized hemoglobin by red-cell distribution width (RDW) product improves resting radial-pulse prediction beyond flexible additive routine measures. Models fitted in 3980 NHANES 2005–2006 adults were transferred without target fitting to 5016 adults in 2007–2008. Target survey-weighted MSE changed by −0.009915 beats²/min² (0.0073% reduction); fixed-model design-bootstrap 95% interval −0.04234 to 0.02344. A source-refit/target design bootstrap gave a much wider interval, −5.453 to 14.893, indicating fitting instability. Quantile-knot and sex-slope challenges also failed to establish a benefit. This negative representation test uses separate cross-sectional samples in one survey system, not independent clinical-system validation, and does not negate anemia-related cardiovascular physiology.
